summary: The backend is one uvicorn worker on one SQLite file (WAL on). It holds together at the route layer, but there is no real migration story and 15 method+path pairs are registered twice. init_db() only runs create_all() plus a hardcoded ALTER list wrapped in `except Exception: pass` (server/database.py:633-712); on a scratch DB I proved a model column with no matching ALTER stays absent and every ORM query then dies with OperationalError: no such column. The worst duplicate is DELETE /api/user/account: routes_user_settings.py:1003 is matched before privacy.py:98 and omits universal_dump_items, so db.delete(user) raises FOREIGN KEY constraint failed and GDPR erasure 500s for the 6/15 prod users with dumped files. Stripe webhooks re-credit on every retry (no event idempotency; payments.provider_ref is not unique; prod has four identical cashapp_1_4000 rows), and two write paths hold the SQLite write lock across LLM awaits.

findings.title: No real migrations: a model change on an existing prod DB breaks at first query, silently
findings.symptom: After adding a model column with no matching hand-written ALTER, the live API 500s on every request touching that table with 'no such column', with no startup error and no migration record.
findings.root_cause: server/database.py:633-634 init_db() runs only Base.metadata.create_all(engine), which creates missing tables and never alters existing ones. The only evolution is a hand-maintained ALTER if-chain (server/database.py:640-708) inside one try/except (639, 711-712). A model column with no hand-added ALTER never exists; a single throwing statement skips the rest of the chain and the error is discarded.
evidence: server/database.py:633-634, 640-708, 711-712 — create_all + hardcoded ALTERs + `except Exception: pass`

measured /tmp/h4/migration_proof.py: old-style users table + init_db() -> notifications_paused present=False; then 'ORM query FAILED: OperationalError (sqlite3.OperationalError) no such column: users.telegram_id'
measured read-only: model-vs-prod column diff over all 32 tables -> 0 missing, so the mechanism is unsound but not drifted today
findings.impact: Every future schema change is an outage gated on remembering to hand-edit a list. No version table, no downgrade, no CI guard; the failure mode is a 500, not a startup abort.

findings.title: GDPR account deletion is shadowed by a duplicate handler and 500s for any user with a dump item
findings.symptom: A user with an uploaded file clicks Delete account, gets a 500, and nothing is erased. Prod: 6 of 15 users have universal_dump_items rows.
findings.root_cause: DELETE /api/user/account is registered twice; include_router(user_settings_router) at server/main.py:378 precedes include_router(privacy_router) at :395, so routes_user_settings.py:1003 wins and privacy.py:98 never runs. The winner deletes 13 tables then db.delete(user) but omits UniversalDumpItem (its own comment at :1019 admits it), and UniversalDumpItem.user_id is FK users.id with no ondelete (server/database.py:595) under PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON (:37).

server/routes_user_settings.py:1003-1034 and :1019; server/privacy.py:43-56 _CHILD_TABLES includes UniversalDumpItem+ApiUsageLog but is unreachable

findings.impact: Broken Art. 17 erasure for a third of the user base and a 500 in the privacy UI, while the correct implementation sits unused one file away.

findings.title: Stripe webhook is not idempotent and Payment.provider_ref is not unique, so retries double-credit
findings.symptom: Stripe re-delivers an event (it retries for days) and the user is credited TIER_CREDITS again, or the renewal is added twice. Nothing notices.
findings.root_cause: server/payments.py:125 handle_stripe_webhook never checks event['id']: checkout.session.completed credits at :162 and invoice.payment_succeeded credits again at :186-197 (credits at :192). process_successful_payment does guard (:324-326) but the webhook does not use it. provider_ref has no unique index (server/database.py:309) and is minted non-uniquely at :255.
evidence: server/payments.py:143-184 (credits at :162) and :186-197 (credits at :192) — no idempotency key
server/payments.py:255 provider_ref = f"{provider}_{user.id}_{amount_cents}"; server/database.py:309 no unique/index
measured read-only prod: SELECT provider_ref,COUNT(*) FROM payments GROUP BY provider_ref HAVING COUNT(*)>1 -> ('cashapp_1_4000', 4), four identical rows for user 1 at 2026-08-18 02:46:30-33
findings.impact: Direct money loss on every retry of a public unauthenticated endpoint; the duplicate prod rows prove double-recording already happens.

findings.title: SQLite write lock held across LLM/HTTP awaits (flush then await then commit)
findings.symptom: Under concurrency, unrelated writes stall up to busy_timeout (30 s) then fail with 'database is locked', though the failing request did nothing slow.
findings.root_cause: server/routes_dump.py:342-343 db.add(assignment); db.flush() opens a write transaction and takes SQLite's RESERVED lock, then awaits classify_assignment_meta at :346 and only commits at :554 after more awaits; batch_finalize repeats this per item. server/routes_import_url.py:135-136 flushes, awaits at :138, commits at :177.
evidence: server/routes_dump.py:342-346, 490-554, 628-631 — flush before await before commit, per batch item
server/routes_import_url.py:135-138,177 — same shape
server/database.py:36 — busy_timeout=30000, so the stall is 30 s before the error
external: FastAPI+SQLite 'database is locked' analysis — writer-writer contention and deferred read-then-write snapshots; mitigate with BEGIN IMMEDIATE / short transactions
findings.impact: One slow LLM batch freezes every other write (login, credit charges, turn-in) for the whole single-worker server; there is no escape valve.

findings.title: PRAGMA order defeats busy_timeout; NullPool re-issues the WAL switch on every request
findings.symptom: Intermittent 'database is locked' at connection open, before any application SQL — exactly what busy_timeout is meant to prevent.
findings.root_cause: server/database.py:34 runs PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL before busy_timeout=30000 at :36. The WAL switch needs a brief exclusive lock that SQLite does NOT route through the busy handler, so it can raise SQLITE_BUSY immediately; because NullPool (:26) opens a connection per request the unprotected window recurs constantly instead of once per process.
evidence: server/database.py:23-27 (NullPool), :34 (WAL first), :36 (busy_timeout last)
measured read-only prod: PRAGMA journal_mode -> 'wal' (already persistent, so re-issuing adds risk with no benefit)
external: 2025 FastAPI+SQLite guidance — the journal_mode switch is not covered by the busy handler and must not precede busy_timeout
findings.impact: Rare load-dependent 500s whose message points at the wrong layer; a two-line fix removes the class.

findings.title: 15 duplicate route registrations; several handlers are unreachable dead code
findings.symptom: What an operator reads in admin.py or at the second definition is not what the server serves; a documented response field can be missing live.

GET /api/admin/stats is defined twice in one file (routes_admin_advanced.py:83 and :463) with different return keys, and GET /api/user/academic-levels twice (routes_user_settings.py:64 and :203, the shadowed one also returning default_styles).

server/routes_admin_advanced.py:83 (users/credit_transactions) vs :463 (total_users/total_credit_transactions); server/routes_user_settings.py:64 vs :203
server/privacy.py:98 shadowed by routes_user_settings.py:1003 (see H4-F2)

findings.title: No request correlation, no alerting, and a health check that hides a dead DB
findings.symptom: A user reports a failure and there is no way to trace their request; if the DB is unreachable /api/health still returns 200 and monitors stay green.
findings.root_cause: server/access_log.py:47-52 formats only time/level/message — no request id, no user — and no contextvar/correlation-id plumbing exists anywhere. Uncaught errors are logged to a file (server/main.py:247-259) with no human alert path (monitors.py has no notify hook). /api/health catches DB exceptions and returns them in the body while still sending 200 (server/main.py:579-600).

findings.title: Synchronous HTTP and DB work on the event loop
findings.symptom: One slow hygiene call freezes the whole API (including /api/health) for up to 4 minutes; every 60 s the monitors snapshot blocks the loop.
findings.root_cause: server/routes_hygiene.py:44 calls sync httpx.post(..., timeout=240.0) inside async def _forward and :31 calls sync httpx.get inside async def status; both run on the event-loop thread. server/monitors.py:217-223 calls sync snapshot_once() in the async loop; it runs six COUNT(*) queries (:107-125) plus line-by-line JSONL reads (:89-105).
evidence: server/routes_hygiene.py:31,44 — sync httpx inside async handlers
server/monitors.py:39,89-105,107-125,217-226 — MONITORS_INTERVAL=60, sync snapshot in async loop
app runs a single uvicorn worker, so a blocked loop blocks everything
findings.impact: A pathological request can self-DoS the server; plus a periodic latency spike as data grows. Fixes are one line each (AsyncClient, asyncio.to_thread).

findings.title: Timestamps stored naive while some writers use local time
findings.symptom: Rows written by different paths carry times hours apart for the same instant; ordering and 24 h metrics mix them.
findings.root_cause: All models use DateTime without timezone=True (server/database.py:74,117,131,150,175,...) while utcnow() returns a tz-aware UTC datetime (:44-45), so SQLite stores an offset-less string. Some writers use local datetime.now(): server/routes_overlord.py:586,1926,2130.
evidence: server/database.py:44-45,74; server/routes_overlord.py:586,1926,2130
measured read-only prod: SELECT created_at FROM users ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 3 -> '2026-09-14 00:20:07.496034', '2026-09-07 21:50:42.610591', '2026-09-03 20:58:08.718128' (no offset)
server/security.py:236,291 and server/trial_service.py:63 bind aware datetimes into the same naive columns
findings.impact: Quiet corruption of the field every audit, export and retention decision depends on.

Unbounded .all(): routes_dump.py:585 and :628, routes_user_settings.py:474-475, routes_features.py:188, routes_overlord.py:154, routes_admin_advanced.py:321.

findings.title: Foreign keys without indexes; missing uniqueness where it matters
findings.symptom: Child-row joins scan whole tables; duplicate relationship rows cannot be rejected by the database.
findings.root_cause: study_materials.assignment_id, study_materials.transcript_id and transcripts.assignment_id are FKs with no index (server/database.py:257-258,202); agent_actions.assignment_id is a bare Integer (:169). No unique constraint on group_memberships(group_id,user_id), admin_notice_reads(notice_id,user_id) or payments.provider_ref.
evidence: measured metadata scan: FK columns without index = study_materials.assignment_id, study_materials.transcript_id, transcripts.assignment_id
findings.impact: Slower joins as tables grow and duplicates prevented only in application code; a unique index on provider_ref also closes H4-F3's DB half.

external_research.what: FastAPI + SQLite 'database is locked' — WAL, busy_timeout ordering, BEGIN IMMEDIATE, NullPool
external_research.why: Confirms H4-F4/F5's mechanism: one writer at a time; a deferred read-then-write snapshot can bypass busy_timeout entirely; PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL needs an exclusive lock that SQLite does not route through the busy handler, so it must not run before busy_timeout. Also supports keeping NullPool for file-backed SQLite.

external_research.what: Alembic batch migrations for SQLite (op.batch_alter_table, render_as_batch, add_column short-circuit, orphan _alembic_tmp tables)
external_research.why: The mechanics for H4-X1: on SQLite a batch block containing only add_column still emits a native ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN (safe on live data); recreate='always' is required for CURRENT_TIMESTAMP/PK/UNIQUE; unnamed constraints are dropped on recreate (name them first); a crashed recreate can leave an orphaned _alembic_tmp_<table>.

external_research.what: Structured logging and correlation IDs in FastAPI (asgi-correlation-id + structlog; middleware ordering; clear_contextvars)
external_research.why: The pattern for H4-X8: add CorrelationIdMiddleware LAST so it is outermost, bind correlation_id into every record, clear contextvars per request. Fits the existing stdlib rotating-file handlers without a rewrite.

external_research.what: Stripe webhook delivery semantics and idempotency
external_research.why: Backs H4-F3: Stripe delivers at least once and may retry for days, and documents deduplicating by event id. Helpotron credits the account on every delivery with no event ledger.

open_questions: Does any client actually call the shadowed /api/user/academic-levels shape that returns default_styles, or /api/admin/stats with the admin_advanced key names? Reading web/src/api.js and the extension call sites settles which copy H4-X6 should delete.
